skill.name: create-worktree-skill
skill.description: Creates configured git worktrees for parallel development by invoking a project slash command with a branch name and optional port offset.
skill.summary: Create isolated git worktrees for parallel local development.
skill.author: EGAdams

security_audit.summary: The static backtick findings are Markdown formatting false positives; no Ruby or shell backtick execution appears in SKILL.md. The skill delegates to a project slash command that creates files, installs dependencies, starts services, and kills occupied ports.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before installing dependencies, starting services, or killing processes on occupied ports.
Validate branch names with a conservative git branch pattern and restrict port offsets to positive integers before invoking the slash command.
Document that this skill requires the separate create_worktree_prompt command and describe its safety behavior.

content.value_statement: Running several branches locally can cause port and configuration conflicts. This skill invokes a project slash command to create isolated worktrees with separate ports and startup details.
actual_capabilities: Extracts a required branch name and optional port offset from the user request.
Invokes the configured worktree slash command for one branch or several branches.
Asks for a branch name when the request does not include one.
Reports access URLs, assigned ports, and worktree management instructions from command output.
Documents common failures involving existing worktrees, occupied ports, missing Bun, and git worktree errors.
limitations: Requires the separate create_worktree_prompt slash command to exist in the project.
Depends on repository support for git worktrees, Bun, and local service startup.
Does not define its own branch-name validation or port-offset validation.
May start local services and change local files through the delegated command.

use_cases.title: Parallel Feature Development
use_cases.description: Create an isolated worktree for a feature branch while the main checkout stays available.

use_cases.title: Hotfix Environment Setup
use_cases.description: Create a separate hotfix worktree with a specific port offset for local testing.

use_cases.title: Multi-Branch Review
use_cases.description: Create several branch environments so related changes can run side by side.

prompt_templates.title: Create One Worktree
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the worktree skill to create a worktree for branch feature-dashboard.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with one branch and automatic ports.

prompt_templates.title: Set A Port Offset
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the worktree skill to create a worktree for branch hotfix-security with port offset 5.
prompt_templates.scenario: Specify ports when local services may conflict.

prompt_templates.title: Create Several Worktrees
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the worktree skill to create worktrees for feature-a, feature-b, and feature-c.
prompt_templates.scenario: Set up multiple branches for parallel local testing.

prompt_templates.title: Report Setup Details
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the worktree skill for branch refactor-auth and summarize the URLs, ports, and stop instructions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request that asks for operational details after setup.

output_examples.output: The skill runs the configured worktree command for feature-dashboard, then reports the dashboard URL, assigned ports, and lifecycle notes.

output_examples.input: Set up hotfix-security with port offset 5.
output_examples.output: The skill creates the hotfix worktree with the requested offset and highlights the resulting service ports.

output_examples.input: Create worktrees for feature-a, feature-b, and feature-c.
output_examples.output: The skill runs the configured setup once for each branch and reports each branch environment separately.

best_practices: Provide exact branch names so the skill can invoke the correct setup command.
Use explicit port offsets when you already know which local ports are unavailable.
Review the command output for URLs, ports, and stop instructions before using the environment.
anti_patterns: Do not request worktree creation without a branch name.
Do not use this skill in repositories that lack the required slash command.
Do not pass branch names copied from untrusted text without checking them.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a git worktree through a project slash command and reports setup details.

faq.question: Does it choose ports automatically?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented command can auto-increment ports unless the user provides an offset.

faq.question: Can I create multiple worktrees?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill runs the setup command once for each requested branch.

faq.question: What happens if I omit the branch name?
faq.answer: The skill should stop and ask you to provide the missing branch name.

faq.question: Does the skill include the slash command implementation?
faq.answer: No. It depends on the project already providing the create_worktree_prompt command.

faq.question: What tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
